A witness traverses without locks, projects the dentry to null and the stray dentry to the directory, and journals EPeerUpdate "peer_rmdir" only if it is auth for a subtree-root dirfrag of the directory (otherwise it acks with NOTJOURNALED); the leader journals with had_peers and may early-reply only if no witness journaled. On commit a journaling witness drops the directory's remaining dirty state (clear_dirty_bits_for_stray); abort relinks the dentry.
features.notes: A non-journaling witness still registers peer_commit, so after a leader failure it is resolved like a prepared one; a witness crash loses that in-memory state (namespace-mutations 8).

features.name: RENAME cross-rank two-phase commit
features.summary: Makes a rename atomic when its dentries, inodes or replicas span several ranks.
features.description: Witnesses are every rank replicating srcdn or destdn, the srcdn auth (always last) and the auths of remote-linked source/target inodes; ranks owning subtrees nested under a renamed directory journal the new location even if not auth (forced journaling). If witnesses exist and any dentry on the traces is projected, the leader first waits for the whole log to be safe (need_flush). Each witness receives OP_RENAMEPREP (paths from the common ancestor, stray blob, snaprealm blobs, op stamp, alternate_name), journals EPeerUpdate "peer_rename_prep" with an encoded rename_rollback, applies and acks; the leader journals EUpdate "rename" with had_peers (no early reply), sends OP_FINISH, peers journal the commit and send OP_COMMITTED, the leader journals ECommitted. Aborts run do_rename_rollback on every prepared peer; in-doubt transactions after a failure are settled in resolve.
features.notes: Rollback never restores ctime/mtime because the rollback record's ctime fields are never set (rename 8, confirmed by grep). Witness traversal errors other than retry/ESTALE hit ceph_assert. Latency with journaled peers includes two sequential journal commits plus round trips; remote xlocks/wrlocks cost one round trip each. Recovery through resolve is catalogued by category 01.

features.name: Inode authority and cap migration inside a cross-rank rename
features.summary: Moves a renamed inode's authority and all client caps to the destination rank when the source primary dentry lives elsewhere.
features.description: When srcdn is primary and not auth on the leader, srci is frozen on the srcdn auth and marked ambiguous-auth on every participant (requests wait WAIT_SINGLEAUTH). Before its prepare the srcdn auth sends OP_RENAMENOTIFY to srcdn replicas and CEPH_SESSION_FLUSHMSG to open client sessions with caps on srci (only if the connection has CEPH_FEATURE_EXPORT_PEER), waiting for all acks. It exports srci with its caps in the prepare ack; the leader imports it, force-opens the client sessions (blocklisted clients skipped) and sends CEPH_CAP_OP_IMPORT; on commit the exporter sends CEPH_CAP_OP_EXPORT. Clients handle EXPORT and IMPORT in either order. A directory moved across ranks moves only its inode; its dirfrags stay on the old rank as new subtree roots.
features.notes: Cap import/export message formats belong to category 03 and subtree migration to category 07; this entry is only the rename-specific use. Importing an inode can resurrect closed client sessions (OPENING -> OPEN) for clients holding caps on it (rename 8).

legacy_parts.note: Server::flush_session returning without CEPH_SESSION_FLUSHMSG for a session whose connection lacks CEPH_FEATURE_EXPORT_PEER (bit 37). The 7.3 kernel and current libcephfs advertise CEPH_FEATURE_EXPORT_PEER, so every baseline session with caps on the renamed inode receives CEPH_SESSION_FLUSHMSG. The C++ feature table dates the bit to kernel 3.14, and Ceph clients have it since v0.75.

features.name: SETATTR request: mask, locks, error order and common tail
features.summary: The single op that changes inode attributes when the client cannot apply the change under an exclusive cap.
features.description: args.setattr carries mode, uid, gid, mtime, atime, size, old_size, mask, btime; MClientRequest v6 adds fscrypt_auth/fscrypt_file and a data payload. Mask bits: MODE 1, UID 2, GID 4, MTIME 8, ATIME 0x10, SIZE 0x20, CTIME 0x40, MTIME_NOW 0x80, ATIME_NOW 0x100 (both ignored by the MDS), BTIME 0x200, KILL_SGUID 0x400, FSCRYPT_AUTH 0x800, FSCRYPT_FILE 0x1000, KILL_SUID 0x2000, KILL_SGID 0x4000. Error order: read-only gate -> path errors -> snapshot -EROFS -> MDS-private inode (ino < 0x1000, not root/mdsdir) -EPERM -> fscrypt fields from an old header -EPERM/-EINVAL -> locks (authlock xlock for MODE/UID/GID/BTIME/KILL_*/FSCRYPT_AUTH, filelock xlock for MTIME/ATIME/SIZE/FSCRYPT_FILE, versionlock wrlock for CTIME) -> check_access(MAY_WRITE[|MAY_CHOWN|MAY_CHGRP]) -> growth while full -ENOSPC -> size-specific checks. Common tail for every SETATTR, including an empty mask ("touch ctime"): ctime = op stamp, rctime = max, change_attr += 1, EUpdate "setattr" with PREDIRTY_PRIMARY (parent mtime untouched); early reply allowed.
features.notes: Clients holding Ax/Fx/Fw apply many changes locally and flush them in cap messages instead (category 03); the kernel sends CTIME alone when only ctime must change and no exclusive cap is held. An xlock on filelock revokes Fs/Fr/Fw/Fx/Fl (not Fc/Fb) from every client; an atime-only SETATTR therefore revokes file caps from all other clients (attributes 8 item 25).

legacy_parts.note: The SETATTR branch for MClientRequest messages below v6: -EPERM on an inode with fscrypt_auth and -EINVAL for the FSCRYPT_AUTH/FSCRYPT_FILE mask bits ('fscrypt fields from an old header'). The branch tests the MClientRequest message version. The 7.3 kernel sends message v6 towards an MDS with FS_BTIME and CephFS bits 18 and 20, and current libcephfs sends HEAD_VERSION 6. Messages below v6 come from kernels before v6.6, the CentOS Stream 8 sample (v4) and Ceph clients before 18.x.

features.name: chmod and chown, with set-user/group-ID clearing
features.summary: Changes mode bits, owner and group; clears setuid/setgid when asked or when ownership changes on an executable file.
features.description: MODE sets mode = (mode & ~07777) | (args.mode & 07777) keeping the file type; UID/GID set uid/gid. Without MODE, for a regular file: if UID, GID or KILL_SGUID is present and any execute bit is set, both S_ISUID and S_ISGID are cleared (also when uid/gid are unchanged); otherwise KILL_SUID clears S_ISUID and KILL_SGID clears S_ISGID. Ownership rules (owner-only chmod, privileged chown, chgrp to own groups, S_ISGID clearing for non-members) are enforced by the VFS setattr_prepare or libcephfs may_setattr; the MDS checks only MDS caps, where MAY_CHOWN/MAY_CHGRP matter for uid= grants. authlock xlock revokes As/Ax first; the kernel rewrites the access ACL after a mode change (posix_acl_chmod).
features.notes: The kernel never sends KILL_* bits (the VFS converts privilege removal into a mode change); libcephfs sends KILL_SUID/KILL_SGID on writes. Under uid= grants an owner chmod of a 0444 file fails because SETATTR always asks MAY_WRITE (attributes 3.2).

features.name: Explicit times (utimes) and btime, with time_warp_seq
features.summary: Sets atime, mtime and birth time to client-supplied values.
features.description: MTIME, ATIME and BTIME copy the request values into the inode and increment time_warp_seq, which tells cap holders that times may have moved backwards; ctime = op stamp as for every SETATTR. MTIME and ATIME take the filelock xlock, BTIME the authlock xlock; BTIME is cleared from the mask for request headers older than v4. MTIME_NOW/ATIME_NOW are ignored (libcephfs strips them after its permission check; the VFS resolves "now" itself).
features.notes: btime is exposed through statx (kernel when non-zero; libcephfs) and settable through libcephfs/Ganesha; the kernel does not send BTIME. Explicit times need ownership, UTIME_NOW needs ownership or write permission: enforced by the VFS (may_setattr) or libcephfs.

legacy_parts.note: Clearing CEPH_SETATTR_BTIME and zeroing btime for requests decoded from the legacy 88-byte head (MClientRequest message below v4, the 'request headers older than v4'). The 7.3 kernel and current libcephfs encode the legacy head only towards an MDS without FS_BTIME (bit 59), which the baseline MDS advertises. The legacy head comes from kernels up to v5.10 and Ceph 10.2.x and older. The 7.3 kernel defines CEPH_SETATTR_BTIME but never sets it.

features.name: Size growth through SETATTR
features.summary: Extends a file; the new range reads as zeros because no objects exist there.
features.description: SIZE not shrinking sets size = rbytes = args.size and mtime = op stamp (overriding an explicit MTIME in the same request; also when the size does not change), and recomputes client_ranges for every client with Fw/Fb issued or wanted. The MDS checks neither the file type, nor max_file_size, nor quotas for size changes: clients return -EFBIG and -EDQUOT themselves; growth is refused with -ENOSPC only when the metadata pool is full.
features.notes: The kernel grows files locally under Fx and flushes the size with caps. A SIZE applied to a directory would be accepted by the MDS; clients never send it (attributes 8 item 6).

features.name: Truncate (shrink) with asynchronous OSD truncation
features.summary: Shrinks a file: the metadata change is journaled first, then clients are told and the RADOS objects are truncated in the background.
features.description: A shrinking SIZE (or size equal with fscrypt data) waits while a previous truncate is pending (WAIT_TRUNC), then inode_t::truncate sets size = rbytes = truncate_size = new size, truncate_from = old size, truncate_seq++, truncate_pending++ and journals truncate_start with the EUpdate. After commit every cap holder gets CEPH_CAP_OP_TRUNC (size, truncate_seq, truncate_size) and MDCache::truncate_inode runs Filer truncate with the realm SnapContext and truncate_seq (waiting for a needed snapflush first); its completion journals truncate_finish and wakes WAIT_TRUNC. A log segment with a pending truncate cannot expire; replay restarts unfinished truncates from truncate_start/truncate_finish records. The OSDs use truncate_seq/truncate_size carried by client writes to discard stale data.
features.notes: The kernel applies a TRUNC only if truncate_seq advances and warns if Fr/Fl were not revoked first. A non-ENOENT OSD error asserts in C_IO_MDC_TruncateFinish, and a stuck truncate keeps its journal segment unexpirable (attributes 8 item 16). Only SETATTR SIZE and OPEN O_TRUNC shrink files; cap flushes and recovery only grow size. See also F-STORE-065 (OSD truncation), F-CACHE-006, F-CAPS-016.

features.name: Timestamps from the client clock and change_attr
features.summary: Every ctime and mtime the MDS writes is the client-supplied request stamp; change_attr counts metadata changes for NFS.
features.description: MDCache::request_start copies the request stamp into the op stamp (the MDS clock is used only when the stamp is zero); the kernel stamps requests with coarse real time (SETATTR with ia_ctime), libcephfs with ceph_clock_now(). Targets of SETATTR, SETXATTR, RMXATTR, LINK, UNLINK/RMDIR, RENAME and O_TRUNC get ctime = op stamp, rctime = max(rctime, op stamp), change_attr += 1; new inodes get all four times = op stamp and change_attr 0; parent directories follow F-NS-043. Cap flushes apply ctime and change_attr only if newer. change_attr is exposed as STATX_CHANGE_COOKIE (kernel i_version) and stx_version (libcephfs), the NFS change attribute used by Ganesha.
features.notes: Clock skew: a client with a slow clock cannot move a directory mtime backwards and gives its own new files past timestamps; a fast clock pushes rctime ahead permanently. SETDIRLAYOUT is the one attribute op that updates neither ctime nor change_attr (attributes 8 item 7). libcephfs reports st_ctime as max(ctime, mtime). See also F-CACHE-004 (time fields).

features.name: fscrypt inode fields and last-block truncate
features.summary: Stores the opaque fscrypt context and real size for encrypted files and performs the read-modify-write truncate of their last block.
features.description: fscrypt_auth and fscrypt_file are opaque byte vectors copied from CREATE/MKNOD/MKDIR/SYMLINK requests and from SETATTR FSCRYPT_AUTH/FSCRYPT_FILE (MClientRequest v6); SETATTR with these bits requires a grant with allow * (MDSAuthCaps::allow_all) else -EACCES, and old request headers get -EPERM on an fscrypt inode or -EINVAL for the bits. For an encrypted file truncated to a non-block-aligned size the client sends rounded sizes, the real size in fscrypt_file and a payload = versioned header (change_attr, file_offset, block_size) + re-encrypted last block; payloads over sizeof(header) + mds_fscrypt_last_block_max_size give -EINVAL, a change_attr different from the projected one flushes the journal and returns -EAGAIN (the kernel retries up to 20 times), otherwise the block is stored in fscrypt_last_block, written to the OSD before truncation and cleared at truncate_finish. Symlink targets and dentry names of encrypted directories are stored as given by the client (base64 ciphertext, alternate_name).
features.notes: Bug by code reading: the allow_all() check runs after project_inode() and leaves the rejected projection at the front of the inode's projection list, so later journal entries carry the rejected fields and committed state lags one projection (attributes 8 item 3; not observed on a cluster). Cap flushes set fscrypt_auth/fscrypt_file without the allow_all() check. The in-memory header size is ABI-dependent (32 bytes on x86_64) while the kernel sends a packed 26-byte header. See also F-CACHE-009 (fscrypt fields), F-ADM-020 (allow * gate).

legacy_parts.note: The SETATTR branch for MClientRequest messages below v6 ('old request headers'): -EPERM on an fscrypt inode and -EINVAL for the FSCRYPT_AUTH/FSCRYPT_FILE bits. The branch tests the MClientRequest message version. The 7.3 kernel sends message v6 towards an MDS with FS_BTIME and CephFS bits 18 and 20, and current libcephfs sends HEAD_VERSION 6. Messages below v6 come from kernels before v6.6, the CentOS Stream 8 sample (v4) and Ceph clients before 18.x.

features.name: Layout ops SETLAYOUT and SETDIRLAYOUT (kernel layout ioctls)
features.summary: Ioctl-driven layout changes of an empty file or of a directory's layout policy, predating the layout vxattrs.
features.description: SETLAYOUT (kclient CEPH_IOC_SET_LAYOUT): regular files only (-EINVAL), snapshot -EROFS, -ENOTEMPTY if size != 0 or truncate_seq > 1; each non-zero field overrides the current value (pool 0 cannot be chosen); a named pool newer than the MDS map waits for it; a changed layout adds MAY_SET_VXATTR; invalid -EINVAL; filelock xlock; projects layout, ctime, change_attr; EUpdate "setlayout", early reply allowed. SETDIRLAYOUT (CEPH_IOC_SET_LAYOUT_POLICY): -ENOTDIR for non-directories; starts from the own, inherited or default layout; projects only layout and version (no ctime/change_attr), no early reply. Both are gated by the full-pool check.
features.notes: Bug by code reading: SETLAYOUT records the old pool with a backtrace version that makes is_backtrace_updated() false, so no backtrace is written to the new pool until a later op dirties it (attributes 8 item 8). The same changes are available through layout vxattrs (F-NS-072).

features.group: Extended attributes, ACLs and virtual xattrs
features.name: SETXATTR and RMXATTR of stored xattrs
features.summary: Sets or removes extended attributes stored as an opaque name/value map per inode, with CREATE/REPLACE semantics.
features.description: Names are routed first: ceph.* vxattr names go to the vxattr path (F-NS-071); other ceph.* names except ceph.mirror.info and ceph.mirror.dirty_snap_id get -EINVAL; any non-ceph name is accepted (namespace rules user./trusted./security./system. are enforced by clients). SETXATTR: snapshot -EROFS -> xattrlock xlock -> check_access(MAY_WRITE) -> size limit -ENOSPC (F-NS-067) -> flags: CEPH_XATTR_CREATE (1) -EEXIST if present, CEPH_XATTR_REPLACE (2) -ENODATA if absent, CEPH_XATTR_REMOVE2 (1<<30) -ENODATA if absent then remove, CEPH_XATTR_REMOVE (1<<31) remove even if absent, 0 create-or-replace -> ctime = op stamp, change_attr += 1, xattr_version += 1, EUpdate "setxattr", early reply allowed. RMXATTR: same routing and snapshot check, -ENODATA if absent, same version bumps, no check_access. The kernel sends RMXATTR for a NULL value with XATTR_REPLACE and SETXATTR|REMOVE otherwise; libcephfs uses REMOVE|REMOVE2 for NULL values and RMXATTR for removexattr.
features.notes: RMXATTR of regular names has no MDS auth-cap check at all, so path, read-only and uid restrictions are not enforced for removal (attributes 8 item 12, code reading). The kernel applies xattr changes locally under Xx and flushes the whole map with caps (category 03). The kernel lists stored ceph.mirror.* names; libcephfs hides every ceph.* name in listxattr.

features.group: Extended attributes, ACLs and virtual xattrs
features.name: Total xattr size limit (max_xattr_size)
features.summary: Limits the combined size of an inode's xattr names and values to a per-file-system value from the MDSMap.
features.description: SETXATTR sums len(name) + len(value) over the projected map (excluding the entry being replaced only when CEPH_XATTR_REPLACE is set) and returns -ENOSPC if adding the new pair exceeds MDSMap::max_xattr_size (default 64 KiB, set with "ceph fs set <fs> max_xattr_size <n>", encoded from MDSMap ext version 18). The kernel reads the same value and falls back to a synchronous SETXATTR when its own framed estimate exceeds it; libcephfs does no client-side check. The limit is not applied to initial xattrs at create, and an oversize blob flushed with Xx caps is silently ignored while xattr_version is still bumped.
features.notes: Without REPLACE, replacing an existing xattr counts both old and new values, and a REMOVE through SETXATTR can fail with -ENOSPC near the limit; the VFS limits single values to 64 KiB (E2BIG) independently.

features.group: Extended attributes, ACLs and virtual xattrs
features.name: xattr blob delivery to clients
features.summary: Sends the whole xattr map of an inode to clients inside InodeStat and cap messages, versioned by xattr_version.
features.description: CInode::encode_inodestat includes the blob (u32 blob_len, u32 count, then per entry u32 name_len, name, u32 val_len, val; or u32 0) when the client has no cap yet, its cap's client_xattr_version is older, or the getattr mask asks for Xs, and keeps it only if Xs is pending or requested; xattr_version is a separate field. The xlocking client or the loner sees projected xattrs. Clients cache the blob under Xs and serve getxattr/listxattr locally; libcephfs forces a GETATTR with Xs the first time ACLs are evaluated.
features.notes: libcephfs with client_debug_getattr_caps aborts if a reply lacks xattrs when Xs was requested (lookup 7.2); batch followers can hit this (F-NS-006).

features.group: Extended attributes, ACLs and virtual xattrs
features.name: POSIX ACLs stored as opaque xattrs
features.summary: Persists system.posix_acl_access and system.posix_acl_default; all ACL evaluation, inheritance and chmod interaction happen in clients.
features.description: The MDS has no ACL code: the two names are ordinary xattrs holding the Linux xattr ACL encoding, set through SETXATTR/RMXATTR and stored verbatim when sent as initial xattrs of CREATE/MKNOD/MKDIR. The kernel (on unless mounted noacl) evaluates them in generic_permission, computes default-ACL inheritance in ceph_pre_init_acls and rewrites the access ACL after chmod; removing an ACL is sent as SETXATTR with CEPH_XATTR_REMOVE. libcephfs handles ACLs only with client_acl_type=posix_acl (empty by default; NFS-Ganesha FSAL_CEPH sets it on every mount).
features.notes: The MDS's own mode-bit test for uid= grants ignores ACLs. pjd-fstest xacl tests run against ceph-fuse with client_acl_type=posix_acl in qa.

features.group: Extended attributes, ACLs and virtual xattrs
features.name: ceph.mirror.* xattrs for snapshot mirroring
features.summary: Stores the mirroring peer identity on the root and a dirty snapshot id used by cephfs-mirror.
features.description: ceph.mirror.info is accepted only on the root (-EINVAL elsewhere); its value must match "cluster_id=<uuid> fs_id=<int>" (-EINVAL otherwise) and is stored as two real xattrs ceph.mirror.info.cluster_id and ceph.mirror.info.fs_id, which removal deletes together; a SETXATTR with REMOVE flags on this name fails with -EINVAL. ceph.mirror.dirty_snap_id is stored with the default handler on any inode. Both take the regular xattr path (xattrlock xlock, early reply allowed).
features.notes: Written by the mgr mirroring module on the peer file system and by cephfs-mirror. libcephfs synthesizes ceph.mirror.info from the two stored xattrs and reads dirty_snap_id after a GETVXATTR miss; the kernel has no table entry and gets -ENODATA from GETVXATTR. See also F-ADM-104 (mgr/mirroring).

features.group: Extended attributes, ACLs and virtual xattrs
features.name: Virtual xattr set/remove path (common rules, p flag)
features.summary: Common handling of SETXATTR/RMXATTR on ceph.* virtual xattr names, which change inode policy instead of the xattr map.
features.description: is_ceph_vxattr matches the prefixes ceph.dir.layout, ceph.file.layout, ceph.quota and the names ceph.quiesce.block, ceph.dir.subvolume, ceph.dir.pin, ceph.dir.pin.random, ceph.dir.pin.distributed, ceph.dir.charmap, ceph.dir.normalization, ceph.dir.encoding, ceph.dir.casesensitive, ceph.dir.subvolume.snaps.visible. handle_client_setvxattr uses only the base ino of the filepath (try_get_auth_inode: -ESTALE if uncached, forward if not auth), checks MAY_SET_VXATTR (MDS-cap p flag, not combined with MAY_WRITE, so root_squash does not apply and "allow rp" suffices), ignores CREATE/REPLACE flags, has no snapshot -EROFS check and skips the quarantine block; each name branch validates and locks (mostly xlock_policylock). Common tail: ctime = op stamp, change_attr += 1, backtrace update for regular files, EUpdate "set vxattr layout"; realm-changing names notify replicas and clients after commit. Policy-changing names get only a safe reply.
features.notes: The individual policies behind quota, pin, subvolume, snaps.visible and quiesce.block vxattrs are catalogued by categories 08, 07 and 10; layouts and charmap here (F-NS-072, F-NS-075). xlocks on policylock/snaplock wait for the whole cluster to be recovered when any replica rank is not active (attributes 8 item 23).

features.group: Extended attributes, ACLs and virtual xattrs
features.name: Layout virtual xattrs (ceph.dir.layout*, ceph.file.layout*)
features.summary: Reads and sets striping layouts and data pools of directories (policy for new files) and of empty files.
features.description: Set: composite "key=value[ key=value]*" (keys stripe_unit, stripe_count, object_size, pool, pool_namespace), single fields, pool_id, pool_name, or .json (object with mandatory object_size, stripe_unit, stripe_count); validated by is_valid_layout; an unknown pool name in .pool/pool= waits for the client's osdmap epoch (args.setxattr.osdmap_epoch) or once for the latest map before -EINVAL, while pool_name and JSON fail at once. Directory layouts (xlock_policylock, no early reply) affect only future creates; removing resets the root to the default and makes other dirs inherit again; encrypted dirs -EINVAL. File layouts need size 0 and truncate_seq <= 1 (-ENOTEMPTY), take filelock, record the old pool and rewrite the backtrace; early reply allowed. GETVXATTR serves pool_name, pool_id and .json (with "inheritance": "@default", "@set" or "@inherited"); clients compute the composite and single-field names from InodeStat.
features.notes: ceph.dir.layout.pool_namespace with an empty value succeeds and, on a dir without its own layout, materializes the inherited layout as its own (code reading). JSON without pool keys resolves to pool 0. GETVXATTR aborts the MDS (ceph_abort) if it reaches the root without a layout. Clients without CEPH_FEATURE_FS_FILE_LAYOUT_V2 get -EIO on access checks for a directory whose layout has a namespace. See also F-CACHE-007 (layout field).

legacy_parts.note: The note's -EIO on access checks for a directory whose layout has a pool namespace when the client lacks CEPH_FEATURE_FS_FILE_LAYOUT_V2 (bit 58). The note restates the Session::check_access branch of F-NS-021. The 7.3 kernel advertises bit 58 under its alias CRUSH_TUNABLES5 and current libcephfs advertises every feature. Kernels before v4.5 and Ceph clients before 10.2.0 lack the bit.

features.group: Extended attributes, ACLs and virtual xattrs
features.name: GETVXATTR op
features.summary: Returns server-computed values of ceph.* virtual xattrs that clients cannot compute from InodeStat.
features.description: A name that is not a vxattr gets -ENODATA before traversal; otherwise rdlock_path_pin_ref(want_auth) without check_access and without policylock/authlock rdlocks; dir-only names on non-dirs and file-layout names on dirs get -ENODATA. Served names: layout pool_name/pool_id/json, ceph.dir.pin, ceph.dir.pin.random, ceph.dir.pin.distributed, ceph.dir.subvolume, ceph.dir.subvolume.snaps.visible, charmap names, ceph.quiesce.block; values come from the projected inode and other vxattr names give -ENODATA. Reply extra_bl = ENCODE_START(1,1) + encoded std::string, no trace; the kernel requires value_len to equal the remaining bytes and only sends GETVXATTR when the session advertises CEPHFS_FEATURE_OP_GETVXATTR (mapping -EOPNOTSUPP to -ENODATA).
features.notes: No access check and projected values: a path-restricted client that knows an ino can read layout/pin/quiesce/charmap values outside its path (attributes 8 item 15, code reading). Clients send GETVXATTR for any ceph.* name missing from their tables; libcephfs then falls back to its cached xattr map.

features.group: Extended attributes, ACLs and virtual xattrs
features.name: Client-synthesized ceph.* vxattrs (InodeStat contract)
features.summary: Most ceph.* names users read (rstats, dirstats, quota, layout, snap.btime, caps, fsid) are computed by clients from InodeStat fields the MDS sends.
features.description: Clients build ceph.dir.entries/files/subdirs from dirstat (getattr with Fs, which rdlocks filelock), ceph.dir.rentries/rfiles/rsubdirs/rbytes/rsnaps/rctime from rstat (getattr with CEPH_STAT_RSTAT, which only forces the auth rank; no nestlock is taken so values may lag), ceph.quota* from the quota field, layouts from layout/dir_layout, ceph.snap.btime from snap_btime, and ceph.caps, ceph.cluster_fsid, ceph.client_id, ceph.auth_mds locally. InodeStat v9 carries ctime, mtime, atime, time_warp_seq, size, max_size, truncate_size/seq, mode, uid, gid, nlink, dirstat nfiles/nsubdirs, rstat rbytes/rfiles/rsubdirs/rctime, dirfragtree, symlink, dir_layout, xattrs, inline data, quota, pool_ns, btime, change_attr, export_pin, snap_btime, rsnaps, snap_metadata, fscrypt fields, optmetadata (charmap, quarantine) and subvolume_id. A set of a read-only name is refused by libcephfs (-EOPNOTSUPP); the kernel marks ceph.dir.rctime and ceph.caps writable, sends them, and the MDS answers -EINVAL.
features.notes: The InodeStat encoding versions are catalogued by category 02; rstat semantics by category 08.

features.group: Extended attributes, ACLs and virtual xattrs
features.name: Case-insensitive and normalized directories (charmap)
features.summary: Directories whose names are case-folded and Unicode-normalized by clients; the MDS stores the setting and refuses CREATE, MKDIR, SYMLINK, LINK and RENAME into such a directory from sessions without CephFS bit 22. The 7.3 kernel sets bit 22 with another meaning and does not fold names, so it is admitted.
features.description: charmap_md_t {casesensitive=true, normalization="nfd", encoding="utf8"} lives in inode_t optmetadata, is set through ceph.dir.charmap removal and ceph.dir.casesensitive/normalization/encoding (only on an empty directory not covered by snapshots, else -ENOTEMPTY; strings not validated), is inherited by new subdirectories at MKDIR, replicated with policylock and sent to clients as InodeStat v8 optmetadata. The MDS never folds names: libcephfs with CEPHFS_FEATURE_CHARMAP (bit 22) sends the folded name as the dentry name and the original spelling as alternate_name; the MDS hashes and orders the folded name and returns alternate_name in LeaseStat v2. CREATE, MKDIR, SYMLINK, LINK and RENAME into a charmap directory return -EPERM for sessions without the feature; MKNOD, lookups and readdir are not checked.
features.notes: Feature bit 22 collision (observed): the scanned Linux tree defines bit 22 as CEPHFS_FEATURE_SUBVOLUME_METRICS and advertises it, so such a kernel passes can_handle_charmap although it does not fold names; the kernel skips InodeStat v8 optmetadata (lookup page 8). The charmap vxattrs lack type and root checks, and an unusable encoding/normalization makes libcephfs fail every new name with -EACCES (attributes 8 items 9 and 27). mgr/volumes depends on the charmap JSON format. See also F-ADM-095 (mgr/volumes charmap).

legacy_parts.note: The -EPERM that Server::can_handle_charmap returns to sessions without CEPHFS_FEATURE_CHARMAP (bit 22) for CREATE, MKDIR, SYMLINK, LINK and RENAME into a charmap directory. The 7.3 kernel sets bit 22 under its own name CEPHFS_FEATURE_SUBVOLUME_METRICS and current libcephfs sets CEPHFS_FEATURE_CHARMAP, so the gate refuses no baseline client. Kernels before v7.1, both CentOS Stream samples and Ceph clients before 19.2.3/20.2.0 lack the bit. The charmap metadata, its vxattrs and the libcephfs name folding are current.

features.group: Extended attributes, ACLs and virtual xattrs
features.name: alternate_name on dentries
features.summary: Stores a second, client-defined name per dentry (fscrypt ciphertext name or the original spelling in a charmap directory).
features.description: CREATE, MKNOD, MKDIR, SYMLINK, LINK and RENAME accept an alternate_name in the request, refuse values longer than mds_alternate_name_max (default 8 KiB) with -ENAMETOOLONG, and store it on the new dentry; RENAME onto an existing dentry with a different alternate_name returns -EINVAL. alternate_name is returned in every LeaseStat v2 (dentry traces, readdir entries, LOOKUPNAME) and travels in rename peer requests.
features.notes: The MDS limits only alternate_name and snapshot names; NAME_MAX for ordinary names is enforced by clients (F-NS-088).

features.name: SETFILELOCK: POSIX fcntl byte-range locks
features.summary: Arbitrates cluster-wide POSIX advisory record locks (F_SETLK/F_SETLKW, also open-file-description locks) in MDS memory.
features.description: Request args filelock_change {u8 rule, u8 type, u64 owner, u64 pid, u64 start, u64 length (0 = to EOF), u8 wait}; rule CEPH_LOCK_FCNTL 1; type SHARED 1, EXCL 2, UNLOCK 4. The op runs on the inode auth, xlocks the internal flocklock (no cap bits correspond to it) and edits the per-inode fcntl table; owner identity is (session client id forced by the MDS, owner) plus pid only when bit 63 of owner is clear. Granting merges/splits the owner's own ranges (one owner's locks never overlap; adjacent same-type ranges coalesce, giving atomic upgrade/downgrade when unopposed); conflict without wait returns -EAGAIN; UNLOCK is idempotent and returns 0. Unknown rules return -EOPNOTSUPP. No check_access is made, nothing is journaled, and SETFILELOCK is never recorded in completed_requests, so a resent request is executed again.
features.notes: No permission check: any session that can name the inode can lock or test it; only the read-only gate and quarantine block apply (lookup page 8). No validation of type, start or length; a same-owner merge computes the end in an int, so ranges ending at or beyond 2^31 merge to a wrong length (flock.cc:452). Kernel OFD locks arrive as FCNTL locks owned by the open file.

features.name: BSD flock whole-file locks
features.summary: Arbitrates flock(2) locks in a table separate from the fcntl locks.
features.description: Rule CEPH_LOCK_FLOCK 2 (CEPH_LOCK_FLOCK_INTR 4 for cancellation) selects the per-inode flock table; clients send start 0, length 0 and the struct file as owner. Semantics, return codes and lifetime are those of the fcntl table except that there is no deadlock detection.

features.name: Blocking lock waits and wake-ups
features.summary: Parks F_SETLKW-style requests in the MDS until the lock can be granted.
features.description: With wait = 1 and a conflict, the lock is added to the table's waiting list, the request drops all locks and auth pins, is marked nowarn (never a slow request) and waits on the inode's WAIT_FLOCK; there is no MDS-side timeout. Any UNLOCK that changed state, removal of a client's held locks on cap removal, and loss of auth (export) wake all WAIT_FLOCK waiters of the inode for both tables, and each retries under the flocklock xlock. Granting a lock or converting EXCL to SHARED wakes nobody.
features.notes: Compatible SHARED waiters stay parked after an EXCL->SHARED downgrade until some unlock happens on that inode; a cap release by a client that only had a queued wait wakes nobody (lookup page 8).

features.name: Lock wait interruption (FCNTL_INTR / FLOCK_INTR)
features.summary: Cancels a parked lock request when the waiting application is interrupted by a signal.
features.description: A client sends SETFILELOCK with rule CEPH_LOCK_FCNTL_INTR (3) or CEPH_LOCK_FLOCK_INTR (4), type UNLOCK and the same owner, pid, start and length; the MDS removes the matching waiting entry (without removing held locks) and wakes waiters; the original request then finds its entry gone and returns -EINTR. A plain UNLOCK of the same (start, length, owner) also cancels a pending wait. If the lock was already granted the INTR removes nothing and the original request returns 0.
features.notes: In the grant-before-INTR race the kernel reports success, while libcephfs returns -EINTR to the caller although the MDS holds the lock until a later unlock or cap removal (lookup page 8).

features.name: fcntl deadlock detection (EDEADLK)
features.summary: Refuses a blocking fcntl lock that would complete a wait-for cycle.
features.description: Before parking a blocking FCNTL request, is_deadlock walks the conflicting holders and, through a process-global map of every waiting fcntl lock on any inode, the locks those holders wait for, up to MAX_DEADLK_DEPTH = 5 hops; reaching the requester returns -EDEADLK. flock locks are not checked.

features.name: GETFILELOCK (F_GETLK)
features.summary: Tests whether a lock could be placed and returns the first conflicting lock.
features.description: Runs on the inode auth with a flocklock rdlock; rule FCNTL or FLOCK selects the table (other rules -EINVAL); look_for_lock returns the first conflicting lock of another owner in ascending start order, or echoes the request with type CEPH_LOCK_UNLOCK. The reply has no trace and carries the 41-byte raw ceph_filelock (start, length, client, owner, pid, type) as extra_bl; the kernel negates the pid and converts start + length to fl_end. No check_access.

features.name: Lock cleanup on cap removal and session end
features.summary: Releases a client's file locks when its capability on the inode goes away, including on eviction.
features.description: CInode::remove_client_cap calls remove_all_from(client) on both tables and wakes waiters if held locks were removed; this covers cap release, session close, eviction and blocklisting (every cap is removed), and cap teardown on export. Clients then mark their local locks lost (kernel CEPH_I_ERROR_FILELOCK, libcephfs I_ERROR_FILELOCK) and fail later lock calls and I/O with -EIO. A stale session only has its caps revoked, so its locks stay until eviction. Locks are not persistent: they live only in CInode memory and also vanish when the inode leaves the cache or the MDS restarts.
features.notes: A lock whose owner holds no cap on the inode survives the owner's session end, and because locks do not pin the inode a lock can vanish silently when the inode is trimmed; clients avoid both by keeping a cap (kernel trim_caps_cb never trims the auth cap while i_filelock_ref > 0). Session reclaim (MClientReclaim, intended for Ganesha HA) kills the old session and thereby drops its locks. Export of lock tables with the inode belongs to category 07.

features.name: Lock reinstatement after an MDS restart
features.summary: Rebuilds held fcntl and flock locks from the clients' reconnect messages.
features.description: Each cap record in MClientReconnect (v2+) carries flockbl = u32 n_fcntl, ceph_filelock[n], u32 n_flock, ceph_filelock[n]; Server::recover_filelocks inserts them into held_locks verbatim (no conflict check, no merge), forcing client to the session id, but only for inodes that are cached and auth when the reconnect is processed. Waiting locks are not in reconnect: clients resend pending SETFILELOCK requests, which the MDS executes afresh once active. The kernel sends both counts 0 when it already flagged lock errors.
features.notes: Recovery gaps observed in code: inodes loaded later in rejoin (process_imported_caps, open-file-table prefetch) and, with several ranks, inodes cached as replicas get their caps back but not their locks; kernel whole-file locks arrive with finite lengths. A legacy flockbl in MClientCaps is also imported by Locker::_do_cap_update (current clients send it empty). The reconnect message format is catalogued by category 02. Each ceph_filelock record is a raw 41-byte struct; the blob is decoded under mds_lock without a try block. Because open files are tracked by the OpenFileTable and EOpen events are not re-journaled after segment expiry, whether a lock survives a failover depends on whether the inode happened to be cached from the replayed journal when the reconnect was processed (resolve-and-rejoin section 8, derived from code). After losing a session while holding locks the kernel fails further lock calls with -EIO until all local locks are released; libcephfs sends an empty blob for inodes that never had lock state and flags I_ERROR_FILELOCK after session loss. Ganesha lock owners are process addresses with pid 0, so locks of a previous Ganesha incarnation go away with the old session when the successor reclaims it (libcephfs-fuse-ganesha 8). See also F-PROTO-056 (reconnect encoding), F-CLU-082 (cap recording).

legacy_parts.note: Locker::_do_cap_update inserting fcntl and flock locks from a non-empty flockbl in MClientCaps (the 'legacy flockbl' of the notes). The 7.3 kernel writes a flock length of 0 in every MClientCaps, and current libcephfs fills flockbl only in MClientReconnect cap records. No examined client sends a non-empty MClientCaps flockbl (kernels v4.4, v4.12, the CentOS Stream 8 sample and 7.3; libcephfs 10.2.0, 12.2.0 and main). The import comes from a 2010 design in which clients sent lock state in cap messages on reconnect (commit fa058c414c1).
evidence_notes: git fa058c414c1 (2010-05-12, mds: handle file locking in MClientCaps on a reconnect)

features.name: Directory link count and size presentation
features.summary: Clients present POSIX-style directory link counts and sizes computed from MDS counters; the MDS stores directory nlink as 1.
features.description: prepare_new_inode stores nlink = 1 for directories (marked FIXME) and MKDIR never changes the parent's nlink; unlink sets it to 0. The kernel reports 2 + i_subdirs for a directory whose nlink is 1; libcephfs reports 2 + dirstat.nsubdirs for 1, 0 for 0, and calls ceph_abort() for any other value. Directory st_size is the entry count (kernel) or rbytes (libcephfs default client_dirsize_rbytes=true, kernel mount option rbytes); st_blocks is ceil(size/512) for files and 0 (kernel) or 1 (libcephfs) for directories; rbytes of a file equals its logical size including holes.
features.notes: An MDS reporting a directory nlink other than 0 or 1 crashes libcephfs clients (Client::fill_stat). Accurate dirstat nsubdirs (F-NS-043) is what the presented link count depends on. Files count hard links: link increments nlink, unlink decrements it and sets STATE_ORPHAN at 0.

features.name: Access time is not maintained by the MDS
features.summary: atime is stored and settable but never updated on reads.
features.description: Kernel mounts set SB_NOATIME | SB_NODIRATIME; libcephfs never assigns atime in its read path; the MDS sets atime only at creation, on SETATTR ATIME and on Fx cap flushes; a forward atime change flushed under Fw alone is dropped; READDIR updates no directory atime. fstests marks atime tests "not run" for ceph and ceph-fuse ("atime not maintained").
features.notes: Documented in doc/cephfs/posix.rst lines 43-47.

features.name: Timestamp range limited to unsigned 32-bit seconds
features.summary: Times before 1970 or after 2106 cannot be represented.
features.description: Seconds are unsigned 32-bit in utime_t and in the wire ceph_timespec; the kernel sets s_time_min = 0, s_time_max = U32_MAX and 1 ns granularity. fstests _require_negative_timestamps marks such tests "not run" for ceph.

features.name: Limits enforced only by clients, and no hard-link limit
features.summary: NAME_MAX, maximum file size and quotas are checked by clients; nobody enforces EMLINK.
features.description: The MDS has no name-length limit for ordinary names (the kernel returns -ENAMETOOLONG above 255 bytes in atomic_open and lookup, libcephfs in _lookup); it limits only alternate_name and snapshot names. max_file_size (MDSMap, default 1 TiB) is enforced as -EFBIG by clients only. Quotas (EDQUOT, EXDEV for rename across quota realms) are enforced by clients only and are approximate. nlink is a signed 32-bit field with no EMLINK check in the MDS or the kernel client (no s_max_links).
features.notes: Quota enforcement and the realm rules are catalogued by category 08.

features.name: Unsupported Linux extensions: renameat2 flags and O_TMPFILE
features.summary: RENAME_NOREPLACE, RENAME_EXCHANGE, RENAME_WHITEOUT and O_TMPFILE are not available; no MDS op exists for them.
features.description: The kernel ceph_rename returns -EINVAL for any renameat2 flag (the VFS returns -EEXIST first for RENAME_NOREPLACE with an existing target); ceph-fuse returns -EINVAL ("cephfs does not support renameat2 flavors"); the libcephfs API has no flags and the RENAME request has no flag field. ceph_dir_iops has no .tmpfile, so O_TMPFILE gets -EOPNOTSUPP from the VFS; xfstests generic/531 (many unlinked O_TMPFILE files) is in the qa exclude list.

features.name: Data-path coherency departures outside the MDS
features.summary: File-data behaviours that differ from POSIX and are decided by clients and OSDs, with the MDS only choosing lock states.
features.description: O_APPEND is not atomic between clients writing concurrently (both compute end of file before obtaining caps; with several writers filelock is LOCK_MIX, granting Fr Fw Fl but neither Fs nor Fx). Writes spanning object boundaries are split into separate OSD operations and are not atomic for concurrent readers/writers. Shared writable mmap is not coherent across hosts (page faults fill the page cache without Fc/Fl). LazyIO (CEPH_O_LAZY, ceph_lazyio, CEPH_IOC_LAZYIO) wants Fl and relaxes coherency on request. O_SYNC/O_DSYNC are handled by clients; libcephfs O_SYNC flushes only the data range. Coherency otherwise comes from cap revocation driven by MDS lock states (no close-to-open semantics).
features.notes: O_APPEND and mmap findings are derived from code, not tested (posix-semantics-contract 3.3.1, 7.2 row 5). The cap model and lock states are catalogued by category 03.

features.name: statfs is answered by the monitors
features.summary: Capacity reporting never involves the MDS except for a quota-root GETATTR from libcephfs.
features.description: Clients send MStatfs to the monitors (MgrStatMonitor::preprocess_statfs) for the single data pool or the cluster; they report 4 MiB blocks, f_ffree = -1, f_namelen 255, f_files = RADOS object count (kernel) or rfiles + rsubdirs of the quota root (libcephfs), and substitute max_bytes quota and rbytes for mounts below a byte quota (kernel unless noquotadf, switching to 4 KiB blocks below 4 MiB; libcephfs with client_quota_df, sending a GETATTR of the quota root on each call).
features.notes: See also F-SNAP-048 (quota-based statfs).

features.name: Conformance suites in the tree (pjd-fstest, xfstests)
features.summary: The POSIX acceptance tests the qa suites run against CephFS and the cases they exclude.
features.description: qa/workunits/suites/pjd.sh downloads pjd-fstest 20090130-RC-aclfixes and runs prove -r as root; it is used by fs/permission (ceph-fuse with client acl type posix_acl and fuse set user groups), fs/workload (fuse default permissions false), fs/thrash, fs/32bits and fs/fscrypt suites; its test directories map to the calls in the POSIX contract table (chflags tests exit early on Linux). xfstests runs with FSTYP=ceph or ceph-fuse; xfstests_dev.py writes a ceph.exclude listing ceph/001, generic/003 (atime options), generic/075 (fsx), generic/538 (unaligned direct AIO) and generic/531 (O_TMPFILE), but only the fscrypt quick-group test passes it to ./check -E.
